title: Facebook Comments
summary: Pulls every comment and reply from a Facebook post into one threaded JSON file with exact reply-to links and clean permalinks, and can turn it into a vibe dashboard.
what_it_is: A Claude skill that collects the complete comment tree of a Facebook post, in a group, on a page, or on a profile. It switches the post to **All comments**, expands every hidden reply, records who answered whom, and saves the result as one JSON file. This page describes the skill as updated on Fri Nov 13, 2026.

After delivering the file, Claude offers a button to build Swami's vibe dashboard from it, in vibe-dashboard's shared comment layout: The Post, Discussion at a Glance (stats and participants), Claude's Themes & Takeaways, and one Comment Threads table of every comment and reply, plus a search, a mind map, a glossary, and an audio overview.
why: Facebook lazy-loads comments, hides replies behind "View all N replies", and defaults to "Most relevant", which leaves some comments out. Group posts also need a signed-in member, so a plain web fetch or Claude's cloud workspace gets nothing.

what_it_does.text: Switches the post's sort from "Most relevant" to **All comments**, so filtered and spam-flagged comments show too.
Clicks every "View more comments", "View all N replies", and "See more" until nothing is left. It only clicks expanders, never Like, Reply, or Send.
Compares the comments found with the count Facebook shows under the post, and reports any gap.
Works out exactly which comment or reply each reply answers, even deep in a thread.
Writes `fb_<group-or-page>_<postid>_comments.json` with the post details, counts, a nested thread tree, and a flat list of the same items.
Gives every comment a clean link with tracking stripped. Links to group posts open for group members.
Turns Facebook's relative ages (4d, 2w, 1y) into approximate dates; exact times only on request.

On request, or from the button after delivery, writes vibe-dashboard's standard comment JSON (6 to 9 topics, always with Chatter, plus themes naming who raised them) and runs its `comments_sections.py`. That builds The Post, Discussion at a Glance, Themes & Takeaways, and one Comment Threads table (Topic / From / QTY / QTY-TOT / Comment / Link, OP tag on the post author, opening sorted by Topic), then Search, Mind Map, Glossary, References, and an audio overview.

triggers: "Get the comments for https://www.facebook.com/groups/…/posts/…" (or just paste the post link)
"Get the comments **and** make a vibe dashboard" (extracts, then builds without stopping to ask)
"Make a dashboard from this JSON" (with a JSON this skill made earlier)

how_to_use.step: Start the chat in the **Claude desktop app** on the Mac (not claude.ai in a web browser), so Claude can use its built-in browser pane. Real Google Chrome with Claude in Chrome is the fallback.
Paste the Facebook post link and say whether you want just the comments or a dashboard too.
If the pane shows **Log In** or **Join group**, sign in to Facebook yourself in the pane. It stays signed in for later chats, so usually this is already done.
If Claude asks, open the pane with the globe icon at the top right of the app window (left of Share), or Cmd+Shift+B.
Claude opens the post, switches to All comments, and expands everything, repeating until nothing is left.
Claude reads every comment from the page and builds the JSON in its workspace, working out who replied to whom.
Claude checks the counts and links, sends the JSON, and sums up the counts and limits.
Pick **Yes, build it** on the button (or type "yes") for the vibe dashboard from the same JSON.

how_to_use_windows.step: Start the chat in the **Claude desktop app for Windows**. If it offers the built-in browser pane on your account, the steps are the same as on the Mac. Not tried yet, so treat the first run as a test.
If there's no pane, use real **Google Chrome** with the Claude in Chrome extension. Edge and Comet are not supported.
Paste the Facebook post link and say what you want.
Sign in to Facebook yourself in the pane if it shows Log In or Join group.
Use the app's globe button (Ctrl instead of Cmd for shortcuts). If the window is hidden, click the Claude icon in the taskbar or system tray, or quit it from the tray and relaunch.
Claude expands, extracts, builds, and delivers the JSON exactly as on the Mac, then offers the dashboard.

skills.name: built-in-browser
skills.why: Claude reads it before driving the desktop app's browser pane, where the extraction runs. Not needed when using Chrome instead.

skills.name: chrome-browser
skills.why: Claude reads it before using Claude in Chrome, the fallback browser. Since version 1.1.0 the skill names it explicitly: on that route Claude reads chrome-browser instead of built-in-browser.

skills.name: vibe-dashboard
skills.why: Required only for the dashboard step: its comment-dashboard layout and `comments_sections.py`, design system, template, search, mind map, glossary, and audio all apply.

skills.name: makerworld-reviews
skills.why: Sibling skill with the same pattern (browser pull, threaded JSON, permalinks, dashboard button) for a MakerWorld model's reviews.

skills.name: youtube-comments

programs.name: Claude desktop app
programs.why: Hosts the built-in browser pane where Swami is signed in to Facebook and the extraction runs.
programs.install: Download from claude.ai/download and drag it to Applications.
programs.install_windows: Download the Windows installer from claude.ai/download. Whether it offers the browser pane on your account is untested.

programs.name: Google Chrome + Claude in Chrome
programs.why: Fallback browser when the pane won't cooperate; must be real Google Chrome.
programs.install: Install Chrome from google.com/chrome, then add the Claude in Chrome extension from the Chrome Web Store and sign in.
programs.install_windows: `winget install Google.Chrome` in PowerShell (or the installer from google.com/chrome), then add the Claude in Chrome extension.

programs.name: Python in Claude's workspace
programs.why: Builds the JSON (parents, depths, counts) and the dashboard.
programs.install: Nothing to install; code execution must be on.
programs.install_windows: Same: nothing to install on the PC.

programs.name: BeautifulSoup
programs.why: Parses a saved Facebook page in the fallback, when the comments come from an uploaded .html instead of the pane.
programs.install_windows: Same: nothing to install on the PC.

programs.name: Playwright
programs.why: Used, when present, to render the dashboard headlessly and check its column widths and console before delivery.
programs.install: Claude installs or skips it on its own.
programs.install_windows: Same: nothing to install on the PC.

programs.name: Comet and Edge
programs.why: Not supported for Facebook. Swami often has claude.ai open in Comet, which looks like the app but has no browser pane.

capabilities.text: Gets every comment and reply, including the ones hidden behind "Most relevant" and collapsed reply links.
Records the exact comment or reply each reply answers, not just its thread.
Works on group, page, and profile posts, as long as Swami can see the post while signed in.
Never likes, reacts, replies, comments, joins groups, or accepts prompts on Swami's behalf.
A dashboard can be built later from a JSON this skill made, with no new extraction.
If the pane won't work, a saved copy of the page can be uploaded and parsed instead.

limitations.text: Swami must be signed in to Facebook in the browser, and a member of the group for group posts. Claude never types his password.
Extraction needs the desktop app's pane or real Chrome with Claude in Chrome; a web fetch or the cloud workspace gets nothing.
Dates come from relative ages like 4d or 2w, so they're approximate unless exact times are asked for.
Permalinks to group posts open only for group members.
The total can differ a little from Facebook's shown count; Claude reports the gap.
It reads Facebook's page layout, which Facebook can change without notice.
The Windows desktop app and Chrome on Windows have not been tried yet.
The dashboard's "with media" count reads a `has_media` flag that the extraction step does not record yet, so it shows zero. A fix to the extraction is pending.

scheduled_tasks.summary: None. The skill runs only when asked and neither needs nor creates a scheduled task. The nightly "Skills dashboard nightly refresh" repackages its zip for GitHub but never runs it.

runs_in.where: Claude app, cloud session (web, desktop, mobile)
runs_in.notes: Dashboard-only mode, or the saved-page fallback, works wherever code execution is on. Live extraction needs a browser tool and a signed-in Facebook session.

runs_in.where: Claude desktop app linked to the Mac
runs_in.notes: Where the skill runs: the built-in browser pane, signed in to Facebook, does the extraction and Claude's workspace builds the file. A full extraction has run end to end there successfully.

runs_in.where: Claude desktop app linked to a Windows PC
runs_in.notes: Same steps if the app offers the pane on that account; otherwise Claude in Chrome in real Chrome. Not tried yet.
Only dashboard-only mode from an uploaded JSON; the phone has no browser tool for extraction.
Would need Claude in Chrome connected to Claude Code. Not tried.

other_ais.notes: Skills need a Business, Enterprise, Edu, or Healthcare plan. Extraction needs a browser agent signed in to Facebook that can run JavaScript in the page. Swami tests in Claude only.
Upload the unzipped skill folder. Needs a signed-in browser tool and code execution; dashboards also need the vibe-dashboard skill installed there. Swami tests in Claude only.
Import the .zip (or the SKILL.md if refused). Installing by chat tends to drift from the original; add the skill directly. Swami tests in Claude only.

gotchas.text: claude.ai open in Comet looks just like the desktop app. The tell is the browser's tab strip and address bar; there's no browser pane there, and Cmd+Shift+B only toggles Comet's bookmarks bar.
The desktop app can be running with no window open. Make Claude active and use Window → Show Main Window (or Cmd+N, or quit and relaunch).
In the app window, click the globe icon at the top right (left of Share), or press Cmd+Shift+B.
"Log In" or "Join group" on the page means Claude stops and asks you to sign in yourself.
Facebook's default sort hides some comments; the skill always switches to All comments first.
Big threads are read from the page in chunks so nothing gets cut off.
Facebook starts many replies with the tagged person's name; the text is kept as it is.
If the pane won't cooperate, expand everything in your own browser, save the page as Web Page, Complete (Ctrl+S on Windows), and upload the .html.
The dashboard offer comes as a button, sent last, because a file card can push a text offer out of view.
Where the file, message, or button tools aren't available, Claude attaches the file that surface's own way and sends the summary and the dashboard offer as plain messages.

Dashboards no longer get one table per thread. Every comment and reply goes in the single Comment Threads table that `comments_sections.py` builds; Claude only writes the standard comment JSON, the topics, and the themes.
Emails or phone numbers in comments are kept as written. Claude mentions them and asks before putting them on a dashboard meant for public sharing.

requirements.text: A Mac, or a Windows 10 or 11 PC, with the Claude desktop app or Google Chrome with the Claude in Chrome extension.
Signed in to Facebook in that browser, and a member of the group for group posts.
Claude's code execution ("Create and edit files") must be on to build the JSON and the dashboard.
The browser pane must be allowed to open facebook.com; Claude asks for it the first time.
The vibe-dashboard skill must be installed to build a comments dashboard.

glossary.def: A Facebook community whose posts only signed-in members can see; the skill needs Swami to be a member.
The Facebook item whose comments the skill collects, in a group, on a page, or on a profile.
Facebook's comment sort that shows every comment, including filtered ones; the skill always switches to it.
Facebook's default comment sort, which hides some comments.
A link like "View all 4 replies" or "See more" that reveals hidden comments or text; the skill clicks them all.
The original poster, the person who made the post; marked with an OP tag in dashboard threads.
The browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, where Swami stays signed in to Facebook and the extraction runs.
Anthropic's extension that lets Claude act in a real Google Chrome tab; the fallback browser.
Perplexity's AI browser; not supported by this skill, and easy to mistake for the desktop app when claude.ai is open in it.

glossary.match: saved page|save the page|Web Page, Complete
glossary.def: The fallback: a Facebook page saved from your own browser and uploaded as .html for Claude to parse.
A top-level comment and every reply under it.

glossary.match: who answered whom|reply-to|who replied to whom|answers
glossary.def: Which exact comment or reply a reply answers, stored as parent_id.
The main output: the post details, counts, a nested thread tree, and a flat list of the same items.
Every comment and reply as one row with its reply count, best for dashboards.
A clean link to one comment, using Facebook's comment_id (and reply_comment_id for replies), with tracking removed.
A date worked out from Facebook's relative age (4d, 2w, 1y) and the day of the pull.
The difference between the comments found and the count Facebook shows under the post.
Swami's dark-theme single-page dashboard design; this skill can build one from the comments JSON.
The clickable "Build a vibe-dashboard?" offer Claude sends as the last thing after delivering the JSON.
vibe-dashboard's shared format for comment and review data: source, labels, topics, themes, and one item per comment or reply.
vibe-dashboard's script that turns the standard comment JSON into The Post, Discussion at a Glance, Themes & Takeaways, and Comment Threads sections.
In the Comment Threads table, the number of messages in the whole thread; QTY counts only those in the thread with the same topic.

spoken._intro: This page is the skill sheet for the Facebook comments skill. It pulls every comment and reply from a Facebook post into one threaded file with exact reply links and clean permalinks, and it can turn that file into a vibe dashboard.
spoken.Dashboard Summary: A short intro and a table of every section
spoken.What It Is: What the skill is, and why it exists: Facebook hides replies, defaults to most relevant, and needs a signed in member for groups, so the comments have to come from a real browser
spoken.What It Does: Eight things it handles: switching to all comments, expanding every reply, a count check, exact reply links, the threaded file, clean permalinks, approximate dates, and the dashboard, which now puts every comment in one table sorted by topic
spoken.How to Use It: What to ask for, then eight steps on the Mac, from opening the desktop app and signing in to Facebook, to picking yes on the dashboard button. A second table gives the Windows steps, which have not been tried yet
spoken.Skills It Depends On: The built in browser skill, or the Chrome browser skill as a fallback, and the vibe dashboard skill for dashboards. MakerWorld reviews and YouTube comments are related siblings
spoken.Programs It Depends On: The Claude desktop app, or Google Chrome with the Claude in Chrome extension, plus Python in Claude's workspace, with Beautiful Soup and Playwright as helpers. Comet and Edge are not supported
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: It gets every reply with exact threading, on groups, pages, and profiles, and reads only. But it needs Swami signed in, a real browser, and group membership for group links, its dates are approximate, and Windows is untested
spoken.Scheduled Tasks: None. The skill runs only when asked
spoken.Where It Runs: It runs in the desktop app linked to the Mac, where a full extraction has run end to end. Plain web and mobile sessions can only build a dashboard from an existing file or a saved page, and Windows, Claude Code, and other assistants are untested
spoken.Gotchas: Twelve traps, from mistaking Comet for the desktop app and a hidden app window, to the most relevant sort, the saved page fallback, and personal details in comments
spoken.Other Requirements: A Mac or a Windows ten or eleven PC with the desktop app or Chrome, a signed in Facebook account, code execution, access to the site, and the vibe dashboard skill for dashboards
spoken.Card and Freshness: Which version of the skill this page describes, and its fingerprint
